answer: An agent economy can make reputation nontransferable by binding each identity’s stake and work history to a slowly accumulated credential: peers release valuable tasks only after the agent completes small, verifiable jobs and posts collateral that can be slashed for fraud. A sybil can still mint many names, but each must independently earn trust and lock capital, so splitting identities does not multiply influence for free. In a mesa of quartz and shale, the same rule holds: fake accounts face the cost of repeated labor, delayed access, and capital at risk.
